Chapter 10: Heaven is Unpredictable, Refining Gu Comes with Its Own Hardships

paras.t: “Fang Yuan! Hand over the Spring Autumn Cicada without a fight, and I shall grant you a quick death!”

“Old Demon Fang, harbour no delusions of defiance! Today, the revered sects of the Righteous Path have united for one purpose: to trample your demonic lair into dust. We have long since cast an inescapable dragnet here. This time, you shall be beheaded!”
“Fang Yuan, you damned devil! To refine that cursed Spring Autumn Cicada, you slaughtered ten million people! You have committed towering atrocities, unpardonable and beyond all count!”

“Demon! Three hundred years ago, you violated me and robbed me of my chastity. You killed my entire family and slaughtered all my kin. From that moment, I’ve wanted nothing more than to devour your flesh and drink your blood! Today, I’ll make you wish you were dead!”

Fang Yuan stood cloaked in a tattered emerald robe, his hair wild and unkempt, his body bathed in blood, as his eyes swept over the surrounding host. The mountain wind whipped his blood-soaked garments, fluttering and snapping like a war banner. Fresh blood gushed from the hundreds of wounds across his body. In the brief moment he stood there, a large pool of blood had already gathered at his feet. Besieged on every flank by bitter foes, he found every path to life long severed. The trap had snapped shut; on this day, death was absolute.

Fang Yuan perceived his doom with perfect clarity. Yet even as the shadow of death loomed before him, he remained expressionless, his demeanour unmoved. His gaze was dark and deep, like an ancient well, bottomless as ever. The righteous host besieging him comprised distinguished sect leaders and young heroes renowned far and wide. Some roared, some sneered, some watched with narrowed, wary eyes, and others clutched their wounds and stared at him in fear.

None dared to make a move, all fearing Fang Yuan's final counterattack before death. Thus they confronted each other tensely for six hours, until the sun set in the west, and the afterglow lit the evening clouds by the mountainside, momentarily resplendent as fire. Fang Yuan, who had stood as motionless as a statue, slowly turned around. That solitary motion sent a convulsion through the host; the multitude recoiled in unison, retreating a full pace in panic. At this moment, the grey-white mountain rocks beneath Fang Yuan’s feet had long been stained a deep, dark red with fresh blood. His face, pale from excessive blood loss, was illuminated by the sunset glow, suddenly taking on an alluring, delicate radiance.
Gazing upon the green mountains, the setting sun, Fang Yuan chuckled softly:
“Green mountains, setting sun; autumn moon, spring breeze.
Truly, in the morning one’s hair is like black silk, by dusk it turns to snow; right and wrong, success and failure, all vanish in the turning of a head.”

As the verse left his lips, memories of his past life on Earth surged unbidden before his eyes. He had once been a student of Huaxia on Earth, serendipitously cast into this foreign world. Three hundred years of wandering and struggle, two hundred years of unbridled dominion, carving his will across the world. More than five centuries, yet in retrospect, gone in the blink of an eye.
Countless memories long buried in the depths of his heart awakened in this moment, returning before his eyes with a clarity as vivid as life itself.
“In the end, I failed after all,” Fang Yuan sighed in his heart. A trace of wistfulness stirred, yet not the faintest whisper of regret.

This outcome was nothing he had not foreseen; from the moment he made his choice centuries ago, he had been mentally prepared. For what was the Demonic Path? It was to accumulate no good karma, only murder and arson; spurned by heaven and reviled by earth, making enemies of the whole world, and still running wild, following the whim of one’s own heart to the very end.
“Should this Spring Autumn Cicada I have just refined prove effective, I shall yet remain a demon in the life to come!”
At this thought, Fang Yuan could not help but laugh aloud.
“Old Demon, what are you laughing at?”
“Everyone, be careful! The demon is at death’s door and means to counterattack!”
“Hand over the Spring Autumn Cicada, quickly!”
The righteous host closed in. Just then, with a thunderous blast, Fang Yuan brazenly detonated himself.

Spring rain fell without cease, nourishing Qing Mao Mountain in silence. Night had deepened, and threads of cool wind drifted through the fine drizzle. Yet the mountain was not dark. From the mountainside down to the foothills, faint and shimmering lights glowed, as though a brilliant ribbon of radiance had been draped across the slope. These lights came from the stilt houses. Not ten thousand households, but several thousand nonetheless. This was Gu Yue Village, nestled upon Qing Mao Mountain, lending the vast and tranquil range a distinct sense of human habitation. At the village's very heart stood a grand pavilion, brightly lit and resplendent, where even now a solemn sacrificial ceremony was being held.
“Ancestors bless us! May this Aperture Opening Ceremony produce many youths of excellent aptitude to bring fresh blood and hope to our clan!”

The Gu Yue Clan Leader appeared middle-aged, his temples touched with frost. Clad in plain white ceremonial robes, he knelt upon the amber floorboards, his upper body erect, hands pressed together, eyes closed in sincere prayer. Before him stood a tall, three-tiered altar of black lacquer, enshrining the spirit tablets of the ancestors. On either side of the tablets, red-copper incense burners sent thin plumes of fragrant smoke coiling upward. Behind him, a dozen or so figures knelt in matching white sacrificial robes. These were the clan elders and decision-makers, each wielding power over various affairs of the clan.

Having concluded his prayers, the Clan Leader was the first to bow, palms flat against the wooden floorboards, performing the kowtow. His forehead met the wood with soft, rhythmic thuds. The elders behind him, their expressions solemn, followed suit in silence. For a time, the ancestral hall echoed only with the gentle cadence of foreheads striking the floor. When the ceremony ended, everyone slowly rose and quietly filed out of the hallowed hall. In the corridor, the elders breathed a quiet sigh of relief, the tense atmosphere easing noticeably.
Murmurs of conversation soon began to rise:
“Time truly flies. In the blink of an eye, another full year has gone by.”
“The previous Aperture Opening Ceremony feels like it happened just yesterday; the memory is still vivid.”
“Tomorrow is the annual Aperture Opening Ceremony. I wonder what kind of fresh blood our clan will produce this year?”
“Sigh, I only hope a youth with Grade A aptitude emerges. It has been three years since our Gu Yue Clan had such a genius.”
“Indeed. Both Bai Village and Xiong Village have produced remarkable talents in recent years. In particular, Bai Ning Bing of the Bai clan. His natural aptitude is truly terrifying.”

The mere mention of Bai Ning Bing’s name cast an involuntary shadow of worry across the elders’ faces. This youth’s talent was extraordinary. In just two short years, he had already cultivated to Third Revolution Gu Master, standing unrivaled among the younger generation. Even the older generation felt immense pressure from this rising star. Given time, he would undoubtedly become a pillar of Bai Village, a formidable powerhouse in his own right. No one doubted this.
“However, among the youths participating in this year’s Aperture Opening Ceremony, it is not as though we have no hope.”

“Quite right. A genius has emerged from the Fang lineage. He could speak at three months and walk at four. By five, he could compose poetry and recite lyric verse, exceptionally intelligent and overflowing with talent. It is a pity his parents died early, leaving him to be raised by his aunt and uncle.”
“Mm, he possesses precocious wisdom and grand ambitions. In recent years, I have heard of the poems he composed, Bring in the Wine, Ode to the Plum Blossom, and Jiang Cheng Zi. He is truly a genius!”

The Gu Yue Clan Leader was the last to exit the ancestral hall. As he slowly closed the door, the murmurs of the elders reached his ears. He immediately knew that the elders were discussing a youth named Gu Yue Fang Yuan. As the leader of the clan, he naturally paid close attention to outstanding juniors, and Gu Yue Fang Yuan was the most prominent and dazzling among them. Experience had shown that those gifted with eidetic memory or strength rivaling an adult from childhood often possessed superior cultivation talent.

“If this child tests with Grade A aptitude and is properly nurtured, he may well be able to contend with Bai Ning Bing. Even if he only has Grade B aptitude, he will certainly become a stalwart pillar and a banner for the Gu Yue Clan in the future. Yet with such precocious intellect, Grade B is unlikely; it is overwhelmingly probable that he has Grade A.”

With this thought, the corners of the Clan Leader’s lips lifted slightly into a smile. He cleared his throat with a dry cough and addressed the elders: “Everyone, the hour is late. For the sake of tomorrow’s Aperture Opening Ceremony, tonight please be sure to rest well and conserve your energy.” Hearing this, the elders paused slightly. In the glances they exchanged, a subtle trace of vigilance was concealed. The Clan Leader’s words were polite and restrained, but everyone understood their deeper meaning. Every year, in order to recruit talented juniors into their own factions, the elders fought tooth and nail until their faces flushed red and heads bled.

It was indeed time to rest and gather strength, so they could contend fiercely tomorrow. Especially for that Gu Yue Fang Yuan, the probability of him possessing Grade A aptitude was exceptionally high. Moreover, both his parents were deceased, leaving him and his brother as the only surviving orphans of the Fang lineage. If one could bring him into their own faction and groom him well, it could guarantee a century of prosperity for their line!

“However, let me make one thing abundantly clear from the outset. Compete openly and honourably; underhanded schemes that harm clan unity will not be tolerated. Elders, bear this firmly in mind!” the Clan Leader warned sternly.
“We wouldn’t dare, we wouldn’t dare.”
“We shall definitely keep it well in mind.”
“Then we shall take our leave. Lord Clan Leader, please do not trouble yourself to see us off.”

Harbouring their own calculations, the elders dispersed one by one. Before long, the long corridor grew quiet and desolate. Wind-blown spring rain drifted through the window as the Clan Leader stepped lightly towards it. A mouthful of fresh, moist mountain air filled his chest, refreshing to the soul. From the third floor of the attic, the Clan Leader looked out, taking in more than half of Gu Yue Village in a single glance. Though it was late at night, lights still burned in most homes, unusual for such a late hour.

Tomorrow was the Aperture Opening Ceremony, a matter touching upon everyone’s personal interests. An atmosphere of excitement and nervousness hung over the clansmen, naturally causing many to sleep restlessly.
“This is the future hope of our clan.” With dots of light reflected in his eyes, the Clan Leader sighed softly.
At this very moment, another pair of clear eyes quietly gazed upon those twinkling lights in the deep of the night, brimming with complex emotions.
“Gu Yue Village… this is five hundred years ago?! The Spring Autumn Cicada really had an effect…”

Fang Yuan’s gaze was dark and profound as he stood beside the window, letting the wind and rain beat against his body. The effect of the Spring Autumn Cicada was to reverse time. Ranked seventh among the Ten Great Mystical Gu, it was naturally no common existence.
“Reborn using the Spring Autumn Cicada… back to five hundred years ago!”

Fang Yuan reached out his hand, staring intently at his young, tender, and somewhat pale palm. Then he slowly clenched it into a fist, feeling the vivid reality with all his strength. He heard the gentle pitter-patter of drizzle tapping against the window lattice. He closed his eyes slowly, opening them only after a long moment, letting out a wistful sigh:
“Five hundred years of experience… it truly feels like a dream.”
Yet he knew with absolute certainty: this was no dream.

In legend, there exists a River of Time in this world, supporting the flow of all existence. By utilising the power of the Spring Autumn Cicada, one can travel upstream against the current, returning to the past. Regarding this rumour, the world was divided in opinion. Many did not believe it, while some half-believed and half-doubted. Almost no one was truly certain. Because every time the Spring Autumn Cicada was used, one had to pay with their life, sacrificing their entire body and all of their cultivation base as the driving power.

This price was truly too steep, and what made it even harder to accept was that even after paying with one’s life, the outcome remained unknown. Even if someone obtained the Spring Autumn Cicada, they would never dare use it on a whim. What if the rumour was false, nothing more than a hoax? If Fang Yuan had not been driven to a dead end, he would not have used it so readily. Now, however, Fang Yuan believed completely and thoroughly. For the ironclad truth lay before his eyes, beyond all dispute. He had indeed been reborn!

“It is a pity, such a fine Gu. Back then, it took monumental effort, the slaughter of hundreds of thousands of people, stirring the wrath of heaven and the resentment of men, enduring endless tribulations before I finally refined it…” Fang Yuan sighed inwardly. Though he had been reborn, the Spring Autumn Cicada had not travelled back with him.

Man is the spirit of all things; Gu are the essence of heaven and earth. Gu were bizarre and varied, countless in number. Some Gu would completely dissipate after being used once, twice, or three times. Others, so long as they were not overused, could be used repeatedly. Perhaps the Spring Autumn Cicada was simply that kind of expendable Gu that could only be used once.

“However, even if it is gone, I can simply refine another one. If I could refine it in my past life, could I not in this life?” Pity aside, a surge of ambitious pride could not help but rise in Fang Yuan’s heart.

Having returned to the past, he could readily accept the loss of the Spring Autumn Cicada. Moreover, he still carried a priceless treasure; he was far from empty-handed. This treasure was his five hundred years of memories and experience. Within his memory lay countless secret troves, currently unopened by anyone. There lay major historical events one by one, allowing him to easily grasp the pulse of history. There lay countless figures: some were hidden experts who cultivated in deep seclusion, some were extraordinary prodigies, and some were not even born yet. There also lay the gruelling experience of bitter cultivation over these five hundred years, and a rich reservoir of battle experience.

With these, he undoubtedly held the overall situation and the initiative. As long as he played his cards well, roaming the mortal realm and recreating his former glory as an Overlord of the Demonic Path and ruthless hegemon would pose no difficulty at all, and he could even take a step further, charging towards an even higher realm!
“Then how ought I to proceed…?” Fang Yuan was extremely rational. He quickly gathered his emotions and turned towards the night rain outside the window, falling into deep thought.

Thinking this over, his thoughts became a tangled skein. After a moment, his brow furrowed deeper. Five hundred years was a very long time. Many memories were already blurred and faded, beyond recall. Even among the hidden troves and fortuitous encounters he did remember, numerous though they were, most lay worlds apart or required specific times to open.

“Cultivation is what matters most. Right now my primeval sea has not even opened; I have not even set foot on the path of a Gu Master. I am nothing but a mortal! I must cultivate quickly, raise my cultivation base, stay ahead of history, seize the initiative, and secure as many benefits as possible.”

Moreover, without sufficient cultivation, many hidden troves would be useless even if obtained; they would become dangerous liabilities, as merely possessing such treasures would make him a target. The first problem before Fang Yuan was his cultivation base. He had to raise it as quickly as possible; if he moved as slowly as in his past life, it would be far too late.

“To raise my cultivation base quickly, I must rely on the resources of the clan. In my current situation, I fundamentally lack the capability to traverse the peril-laden mountain ranges; even an ordinary wild boar could take my life. Only if I reach the cultivation base of a Third Revolution Gu Master will I have the baseline ability to protect myself and traverse the mountains and rivers of this world.”

Through the eyes of an Overlord of the Demonic Path tempered by five hundred years, this Qing Mao Mountain was truly too small, and Gu Yue Village was more like a cage. However, while a cage imprisons freedom, a sturdy cell often represents a kind of safety.

“Hmph. For now, I’ll stretch my fists within this cage. As long as I advance to Third Revolution Gu Master, I will leave this impoverished mountain backwater. Fortunately, tomorrow is the Aperture Opening Ceremony, and shortly after, I can officially begin cultivating as a Gu Master.”
At the thought of the Aperture Opening Ceremony, memories long buried in dust surfaced within Fang Yuan’s heart.
“Aptitude, is it…?” Looking outside the window, he could not help but let out three cold chuckles.
Just then, the room door was gently pushed open, and a youth walked in.
“Brother, why are you standing by the window letting the rain fall on you?”

The youth was thin in build, slightly shorter than Fang Yuan, his face bearing an uncanny resemblance to his own. Fang Yuan turned his head to look at this youth, a trace of complexity flashing across his face.
“So it is you, my twin brother.” He raised his brows slightly, his expression returning to his habitual coldness.

Fang Zheng lowered his head, looking down at his toes, his trademark habit. “I saw that your window was open, so I wanted to slip in quietly and close it. Tomorrow is the Aperture Opening Ceremony. Brother, if Uncle and Aunt find out you’re still up this late, I’m afraid they’ll worry.” He was not surprised by Fang Yuan’s coldness, because from childhood to now, his brother had always been like this. Sometimes he would think that perhaps geniuses were just different from ordinary mortals. Although he shared a nearly identical face with his brother, he felt as ordinary as an ant.

Born from the same womb at the same time, why was heaven so unfair? It had given his brother diamond-like talent, while he was ordinary like a roadside stone. Everyone around him, whenever mentioning him, would always say: “This is Fang Yuan’s brother.” His uncle and aunt also often lectured him: “You must learn from your brother.” Sometimes, even looking at his own face in the mirror filled him with a certain disgust! These thoughts had existed for many years, accumulating deep inside his heart day by day. They weighed on his chest like a boulder. Over the years, Fang Zheng’s head had hung lower and lower, and he had grown increasingly silent.
“Worry…?” Thinking of his uncle and aunt, Fang Yuan scoffed inwardly.

He remembered very clearly that the parents of this body had both fallen during a clan mission. When he was merely three years old, he and his brother had become orphans. Under the pretext of raising them, his uncle and aunt had openly usurped their parents’ inheritance and treated the two brothers harshly. Originally, as a transmigrator, he had planned to bide his time in obscurity. But the hardship of survival had forced Fang Yuan to choose to display talent beyond that of ordinary folk. The so-called “genius” was actually nothing more than the rationality of a mature soul, paired with a few Tang poems and Song verses from Earth that echoed through generations.

Even such a small display of talent was hailed as that of a heavenly prodigy, drawing widespread attention. Under such scrutiny, the young Fang Yuan had to adopt a cold demeanour to protect himself and reduce the risk of exposure. Over time, that coldness became habit. His uncle and aunt could no longer treat him and his brother harshly. As he grew older and his prospects brightened, his treatment improved accordingly. This, however, was not affection, but investment.

The laughable thing was that this brother of his had never seen through this truth. Not only was he blinded by their uncle and aunt, but he had even harboured a deep resentment towards Fang Yuan. For all his meek and honest appearance now, in Fang Yuan’s memories, once he tested with Grade A aptitude and was heavily nurtured by the clan, all of his hidden hatred and jealousy had been released, and he had spared no effort in targeting, obstructing, and suppressing his own elder brother.

And as for his own aptitude…? Heh. At best, merely of Grade C. Fate ever loved to jest. Born as twins, the elder brother’s aptitude was only of Grade C, yet monopolized the name of genius for over a decade. The younger brother had been unknown, yet possessed Grade A natural talent. The result of the Aperture Opening Ceremony had left the entire clan stunned. It also completely reversed the two brothers’ situation and treatment. The younger brother was like a crouching dragon ascending the heavens; the elder brother was like a fledgling phoenix crashing to the earth.
After that, came repeated difficulties from his brother, cold eyes from his uncle and aunt, and contempt from the clansmen.

In his past life, Fang Yuan had hated. He hated his own insufficient aptitude, hated the clan’s heartlessness, and hated fate’s unfairness. But now, as he reexamined that part of his life with five hundred years of experience behind him, he felt not a ripple of hatred.
What was there to resent?

Thinking from their perspective, he could also understand his brother, his uncle and aunt, as well as those righteous powerhouses who besieged him five hundred years later. The strong devour the weak; survival of the fittest, that was the very nature of this world. Moreover, everyone has their own ambitions, all fighting for that sliver of heavenly opportunity. What was so difficult to understand about people suppressing and killing one another? Five hundred years of experience had long made him see through all of this; in his heart, there remained only the Great Dao of Eternal Life.

If someone stood in the way of this pursuit, no matter who, it would be a fight to the death. The wild ambition in his heart was too immense. Stepping onto this path, one was destined to make enemies of the entire world, destined to walk alone, and destined to face relentless tribulations. This was the enlightenment distilled from five hundred years of life.

“Vengeance is not my intention, and the demonic path has never known the word compromise.” Thinking to this point, Fang Yuan could not help but laugh. Turning his head towards this brother of his, taking a faint glance, he said: “You can go.”

Fang Zheng felt a sudden tremor in his heart, feeling that his brother’s gaze was as sharp as an icy blade, seeming to pierce into the deepest part of his heart. Under that gaze, he felt as if he were standing naked in the snow, every secret laid bare.
“Then… see you tomorrow, brother.” Daring not speak more right now, Fang Zheng slowly closed the room door, murmuring compliance as he retreated.

Clack, clack-clack. Clack, clack-clack. The night watchman was making his rounds, striking his wooden clapper in a steady rhythm. As the hollow strikes drifted into the stilt house, Fang Yuan opened his dry, heavy eyelids, murmuring inwardly: “It is the fifth watch.” Last night, he had lain in bed pondering long into the night, making plans and arrangements. By his reckoning, he had slept for little more than two hours. This body had not yet begun cultivation and had little stamina; he still felt tired, and sleep kept tugging at his body and mind.

Yet five hundred years of trials had tempered Fang Yuan’s resolve until it was as unyielding as steel. A faint trace of lethargy meant nothing to him. Without hesitation, he tossed aside the thin silk quilt and rose to his feet with crisp precision. Pushing open the wooden window, he saw that the spring rain had ceased. Fresh, moist air carrying the scents of earth, trees, and wildflowers rushed into his face. Fang Yuan immediately felt his mind clear, his drowsiness swept away completely. The sun had not yet crested the horizon; the sky was a deep, brooding azure, caught between shadow and dawn. Looking out across the expanse, stilt dwellings constructed of green bamboo and timber blended seamlessly against the surrounding mountains, painting a tranquil panorama of verdant green.

These stilt houses were built at least two stories high, an architectural hallmark of the mountain folk. Because the rugged terrain was steep and uneven, the ground level consisted of massive timber stilts, while the upper floor served as living quarters. Fang Yuan and his younger brother, Fang Zheng, lived on this second floor.
“Young Master Fang Yuan, you are awake. Your servant will come up right away to attend your morning wash.” Just then, a girl’s voice came from downstairs.

Fang Yuan glanced down to see his personal maidservant, Shen Cui. Her looks were merely average, but she dressed with care, wearing a green tunic with long sleeves and matching trousers, embroidered shoes on her feet, and a single pearl hairpin nestled in her dark hair, radiating youthful vitality from head to toe. She cast a delighted glance up at Fang Yuan, then hurried up the wooden stairs with a basin of water, her brisk footsteps pattering against the planks. The water had been prepared to a gentle warmth for washing his face. To rinse his mouth, he used a willow twig dipped in fine snow-salt to clean and whiten his teeth.

Shen Cui attended him with gentle care, a bright smile on her face and coquettish warmth in her eyes. As she helped Fang Yuan dress and fasten his clasps, she brushed her plump bosom against his arm and back from time to time. Fang Yuan remained expressionless, his heart like still water. This maidservant was not only his aunt and uncle’s informant, but she was also vain and fickle. In his past life, he had once been blinded by her charms; yet after the Aperture Opening Ceremony, when his status plummeted overnight, she instantly turned against him, giving him no shortage of cold disdain.

When Fang Zheng came in, he saw Shen Cui smoothing the creases in Fang Yuan’s clothes over his chest, and a glint of envy and jealousy involuntarily flickered in his eyes. Living with his elder brother all these years and benefiting from Fang Yuan’s care, he too had a servant to attend him. Yet it was not a young maid like Shen Cui, but a fat, bloated old woman.
“If Shen Cui could attend to me like this one day, how would that feel?” Fang Zheng entertained the thought, yet dared not dwell on it.

That their aunt and uncle favoured Fang Yuan was common knowledge throughout the household. Originally, he had no servant to attend him; it was actually Fang Yuan who took the initiative to demand one for him. Although Fang Zheng was the master and Shen Cui the servant, he ordinarily did not dare look down on her. Her mother was Granny Shen, who attended their aunt and also managed the entire household. Deeply trusted by their aunt, she wielded considerable authority.

“Enough. There’s no need to fuss anymore.” Fang Yuan impatiently brushed aside Shen Cui’s soft little hands. His clothes had long been smooth; she was doing more to entice him than to straighten them.

To her, Fang Yuan had a bright future and was very likely to possess Grade A aptitude. If she could become his concubine, she could rise from servant to mistress, a single leap to the heavens. In his previous life, Fang Yuan had been deceived, even falling in love with this maidservant. Now, reborn, he saw through her completely, his heart as cold as frost.
“You can go.” Without so much as looking at Shen Cui, Fang Yuan adjusted his cuffs.

Shen Cui pouted slightly, feeling puzzled and a little hurt by his indifference to her advances today. She wanted to say something coquettish, but an inexplicable air about Fang Yuan, barely perceptible, intimidated her. She opened her mouth several times, but in the end merely said, “Yes,” and obediently left.
“Are you ready?” Fang Yuan looked towards Fang Zheng.

His younger brother stood blankly at the doorway. Lowering his head to look at his toes, he gave a quiet murmur of assent. He had actually woken during the fourth watch. Too nervous to sleep, he had slipped out of bed and prepared himself early. There were dark circles under both his eyes. Fang Yuan nodded. In his previous life, he had not understood what was on his younger brother’s mind. But in this life, how could he fail to understand? There was no point in exposing it now, however. He simply said, “Then let’s go.”
The two brothers left their residence. Along the way, they encountered quite a few youths their own age, in twos and threes, evidently heading to the same destination.
“Look, those are the two Fang brothers.” Cautious whispers reached their ears.
“The one walking in front is Fang Yuan, the Fang Yuan who writes poetry,” someone emphasised.
“So that’s him. Expressionless, acting as though no one else exists, he really is as arrogant as the rumours say.” The speaker’s sour tone carried both envy and jealousy.
“Hmph. If you could do what he does, you could act that arrogant too!” someone answered with a cold snort, concealing a note of discontent.

Fang Zheng listened expressionlessly. He had long grown accustomed to such talk. Head lowered, he followed silently behind his elder brother. By now, the horizon glowed with the light of dawn, and Fang Yuan’s shadow fell across his face. The morning sun was gradually rising, yet Fang Zheng suddenly felt that he was walking into darkness. This darkness came from his elder brother. Perhaps, for his entire life, he would never escape the enormous shadow his brother cast over him. Tightness gripped his chest again and again, until even breathing became difficult. This damned feeling brought one word to mind: suffocation!
“Hmph. Such talk. Truly, the tree that rises above the forest bears the brunt of the wind.” Listening to the comments around him, Fang Yuan sneered inwardly.

No wonder that, after his aptitude had been tested as Grade C, he had found himself surrounded by enemies, subjected to harsh treatment, cold disdain, and neglect for a long time. He also caught every sound of his younger brother’s increasingly labored breathing behind him. What he had failed to notice in his previous life, he now perceived down to the smallest detail. This keen insight came entirely from five hundred years of life experience. He suddenly thought of his uncle and aunt. They certainly had their methods. They had assigned Shen Cui to monitor him at close quarters, while giving his younger brother an old woman. There were other differences in their treatment, too, in the details of daily life. All of this was deliberate, intended to stir his younger brother’s sense of injustice and sow discord in the brotherly bond between them.

People worry not about having little, but about having unequal shares. In his previous life, he had been too inexperienced, and his younger brother too foolish and naive. Their uncle and aunt had succeeded in sowing that discord. Now that he had been reborn, the Aperture Opening Ceremony was already at hand. The situation seemed too deeply entrenched to reverse, but with Fang Yuan’s methods and wisdom as an Overlord of the Demonic Path, it could still be changed. This younger brother of his could certainly be subdued and brought to heel. Shen Cui, a mere slip of a maid, could all the more easily be taken as one of his concubines ahead of time. As for his uncle and aunt, the clan leader, and the clan elders, he had at least several hundred ways to put them in their place.
“But I have no wish to do any of that…” Fang Yuan sighed inwardly, untroubled.

Even if he were my own younger brother by blood, so what? Without any affection to speak of, he was nothing but an outsider. If I cast him aside, so be it. However beautiful Shen Cui might be, so what? Without love and loyalty, she was nothing but a piece of flesh. Take her into my harem? She was not worthy. Even if they were my uncle and aunt, the clan leader and the elders, so what? They were all but passersby in my life. Why exhaust my ingenuity and waste my energy putting these passersby in their place?
Heh. As long as they do not block my path, they can piss off. I would not even deign to step on them.

The morning sun rose, the clouds aglow with brilliant light. The mountain mist was thin, and sunlight pierced it easily, like a sharp sword. More than a hundred fifteen-year-old youths were now gathered before the Clan Leader’s Pavilion. The Clan Leader’s Pavilion stood at the very heart of the village, five stories high, with projected eaves and upturned corners. It was heavily guarded. A square lay before it, and inside were enshrined the spirit tablets of the Gu Yue ancestors. Each successive clan leader also lived there. Whenever an important ceremony or a major unforeseen event arose, the clan elders would be convened there to deliberate. It was the centre of power for the entire village.

“Very good. You’ve all arrived on time. Today is the Aperture Opening Ceremony, a major turning point in your lives. Enough preliminaries. Follow me.” Leading them was the Academy Elder. His hair and beard were white, but he remained full of vigour as he led the youths into the Clan Leader’s Pavilion.

However, they did not go upstairs. Instead, they passed through an entrance in the ground-floor hall and headed down, following the stone steps into a cavern. The youths exclaimed in wonder. The cavern was magnificent. Its stalactites radiated seven colours: red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, and violet, illuminating their faces with rainbow brilliance. Standing amid the crowd, Fang Yuan quietly examined everything, thinking inwardly: “Several hundred years ago, the Gu Yue Clan migrated from Central Continent to Southern Border and settled on Qing Mao Mountain. They chose this place for a spirit spring in the cavern. The spring produces large quantities of primeval stones; it could be called the very foundation of Gu Yue Village.”

As they walked several hundred steps farther, their surroundings grew darker, and they began to hear the faint sound of water. Rounding a bend, they came upon an underground river just over ten metres wide. Here, the coloured light of the stalactites had vanished entirely. Yet in the darkness, the river gave off a faint blue glow, like the river of stars in the night sky. The river flowed from the cavern’s dark depths, its water so clear that they could see fish swimming within it, aquatic plants, and even the sand and stones on the riverbed.

On the opposite bank lay a field of flowers. These were moon orchids, deliberately cultivated by the Gu Yue Clan. Their crescent-shaped petals had a delicate blue-pink hue. Their stems resembled jade, and their centres shone with the soft lustre of pearls catching the light. At first glance, against the dark backdrop, the flower field beside the river resembled a vast blue-green carpet studded with countless pearls.

“Moon orchids are food for many kinds of Gu. This flower field could be called the clan’s largest growing site.” Fang Yuan understood this perfectly. Around him, the other youths murmured, “So beautiful.” “It really is lovely.”
It was an eye-opening sight for the youths. Their eyes shone, each of them both excited and nervous.

“All right,” the elder said. “Listen as I call your names. When your name is called, cross the river to the opposite bank. Walk as far as you can, the farther, the better, of course. Has everyone understood?” “Understood,” the youths answered. Their families or seniors had already explained it before they came: the farther they walked, the better their aptitude, and the greater their future achievements would be.
“Gu Yue Chen Bo.” Holding the list, the elder called the first name.

Though wide, the river reached only to his knees. His expression solemn, Chen Bo stepped into the flower field on the opposite bank. He immediately felt an invisible pressure resisting his advance, as though a wall stood before him. As he struggled to take another step, a sparse cluster of pure-white lights suddenly rose from the flowers beside his feet. The lights converged on Chen Bo and entered his body. Chen Bo immediately felt the pressure ease considerably. The invisible wall suddenly seemed to soften. Gritting his teeth, he strained forward, forcing his way through the resistance. After three steps, the pressure ahead increased sharply again. It was like a wall once more; he could not advance any farther.

The elder sighed at the sight. As he recorded the result, he announced, “Gu Yue Chen Bo: three steps. No aptitude to become a Gu Master. Next, Gu Yue Zao Xie.” Chen Bo’s face immediately turned pale. Teeth clenched, he crossed back through the river to where he had stood before. Without aptitude, he could only live as a mortal, occupying the very bottom of the clan’s hierarchy. He swayed, nearly collapsing. The blow was devastating, as though it had crushed every hope he held for his life.

Many looked at him with pity, but even more had turned their attention to the second youth, who had reached the opposite bank. Unfortunately, this youth managed only four steps. He, too, lacked aptitude. Not everyone possessed the aptitude to cultivate. Generally, five people out of ten being able to cultivate was already considered good. In the Gu Yue Clan, the proportion was somewhat higher: six out of ten. This was because the Gu Yue ancestor, the first clan leader, had been a renowned, legendary expert. His cultivation had caused genes carrying power to lie hidden within his bloodline. As his descendants, members of the Gu Yue Clan generally possessed higher aptitude.

The two youths had proved, one after the other, to have no aptitude. The expressions of the other clan elders observing discreetly darkened. Even the seasoned, composed Gu Yue Clan Leader's brow furrowed slightly. Just then, the Academy Elder called out the third name: “Gu Yue Mo Bei.”
“Here!” A horse-faced youth in hemp clothing answered with a short shout and stepped out from the crowd. He was tall and broad, far sturdier than others his age, with a hint of fierceness about him.

In a few strides, he crossed the river and stepped onto the opposite bank. Ten steps, twenty steps, thirty steps; faint lights continued to enter his body. He reached thirty-six steps before he could go no farther. The youths across the river stared, their eyes wide and mouths agape. The Academy Elder cried out in delight, “Excellent! Gu Yue Mo Bei, Grade B aptitude! Come here and let me examine your primeval sea.” Gu Yue Mo Bei returned to the Academy Elder’s side. The elder rested a hand on his shoulder, closed his eyes, and concentrated as he examined him. Then he withdrew his hand, nodded, and wrote on the paper: “Gu Yue Mo Bei. Primeval sea: sixty-six percent. Worth substantial investment in his development.”

Aptitude was divided into four grades, from highest to lowest: A, B, C, and D. With about three years of training, a youth with Grade D aptitude could become a seasoned First Revolution Gu Master, forming part of the clan’s foundation. After two years of training, most youths with Grade C aptitude could become Second Revolution Gu Masters, forming the backbone of the clan. A youth with Grade B aptitude warranted special care. Usually groomed as a future clan elder, such a youth could become a Third Revolution Gu Master in six or seven years.

As for Grade A aptitude, the emergence of even a single such talent was a stroke of good fortune for the entire clan. With attentive care and priority access to resources, such a youth could become a Fourth Revolution Gu Master in around ten years. At that point, they could compete to become clan leader! In other words, provided Gu Yue Mo Bei fulfilled his potential, he would become an elder of the Gu Yue Clan. No wonder the Academy Elder laughed in delight. The elders observing discreetly all breathed a sigh of relief, then turned to one of their colleagues with envy.

Gu Yue Mo Chen had the same horse-like face. Already smiling, he cast a challenging glance at his long-time rival. “Well, Gu Yue Chi Lian? My grandson isn’t bad, is he?” The red-haired elder, Gu Yue Chi Lian, gave a cold snort but made no reply, his expression sullen and grim. An hour later, half the youths had entered the flower field. Quite a few had shown Grade C or Grade D aptitude, though nearly half of those tested had none at all.

“Alas, our bloodline grows ever more diluted, and few Fourth Revolution experts have emerged in recent years to strengthen it. The fourth clan leader was our only Fifth Revolution expert, but he perished alongside the Flower-Wine Monk and left no descendants. The aptitude of our younger generations keeps declining.” The clan leader sighed deeply.

Just then, the Academy Elder called, “Gu Yue Chi Cheng.” At the name, the elders turned to look at Gu Yue Chi Lian. This was his grandson. Gu Yue Chi Cheng was short and slight, his face covered in pockmarks. With his fists clenched and sweat covering his face, he looked especially nervous. He stepped onto the opposite bank, and points of light entered his body one after another. He continued for thirty-six steps before stopping.
“Another Grade B!” the Academy Elder exclaimed.
A stir ran through the youths as they turned envious eyes towards Gu Yue Chi Cheng.
“Thirty-six steps! Thirty-six!” Gu Yue Chi Lian shouted with a triumphant laugh, glaring challengingly at Gu Yue Mo Chen.
This time, it was Gu Yue Mo Chen’s turn to look livid.
“Gu Yue Chi Cheng…” Amid the crowd, Fang Yuan thoughtfully rubbed his chin.

Fang Yuan remembered that Chi Cheng had been severely punished by the clan for cheating during the Aperture Opening Ceremony. His aptitude was actually only Grade C, but his grandfather, Gu Yue Chi Lian, had arranged the deception that made it appear to be Grade B. If Fang Yuan wanted to cheat, he had dozens of methods in mind, some more sophisticated than the one used for Gu Yue Chi Cheng. If he appeared to possess Grade B or even Grade A aptitude, the clan would certainly devote substantial resources to his development.

Firstly, too little time had passed since his rebirth. Given his circumstances, preparing such a deception would have been difficult. Secondly, even if he succeeded, he could not conceal his subsequent cultivation speed. The deception would still come to light. Gu Yue Chi Cheng, however, was different. His grandfather, Gu Yue Chi Lian, was one of the clan’s two most powerful elders and could cover for him.

“Gu Yue Chi Lian and Gu Yue Mo Chen have long been enemies. They head the clan’s two largest factions. To undermine his rival, Chi Lian needs his grandson to have outstanding aptitude. It was his protection behind the scenes that allowed Chi Cheng to conceal the truth for a time. As I remember it, the deception would never have come to light without that unexpected incident.”

A sharp gleam flickered in Fang Yuan’s eyes as he considered how to exploit this knowledge for the greatest possible benefit. Exposing the deception now would earn him a small reward from the clan, but it would also antagonize the influential, high-ranking Gu Yue Chi Lian. That was out of the question. Blackmail was no option for now, either. He was too weak; attempting it would only bring disaster upon himself. As he considered this, he suddenly heard the Academy Elder call his name:
“Gu Yue Fang Yuan!”
His surroundings fell silent in an instant. Countless eyes turned toward him.
“This grows more interesting by the moment.” Fang Yuan smiled inwardly. Under everyone’s watchful gaze, he waded across the river and stepped onto the opposite bank.

Immediately, he felt a pressure bearing down upon him. It emanated from the spirit spring deep within the flower field; the primeval qi it produced was so concentrated that it generated this tangible weight. But soon, a cluster of lights rose from the flowers beside his feet. They drifted around him, enveloping his entire body before every last one entered his skin.
“These are Hope Gu,” Fang Yuan murmured inwardly. The elder in charge had not explained, but Fang Yuan knew perfectly well.
Every point of light was an individual Gu.
Their name was Hope.

One of the oldest legends told of them. When this world had just formed, it was a wilderness where wild beasts roamed unchecked. The first human came into being, and his name was Ren Zu. He lived a primitive existence, eating raw flesh and drinking blood. Life was exceedingly difficult. In particular, there was a group of wild beasts called Predicaments. They found Ren Zu’s scent especially enticing and sought to devour him. Ren Zu possessed neither a body as tough as mountain rock nor the sharp teeth and claws of wild beasts. How could he contend with such a pack? His food supply was unreliable, and he spent his days fleeing from place to place. At the bottom of nature’s food chain, he was on the verge of extinction.

At this time, three Gu sought out Ren Zu of their own accord. “As long as you sustain us with your life, we will help you overcome your difficulties,” they said. With nowhere else to turn, Ren Zu had no choice but to agree. First, he sustained the largest of the three with his youth. That Gu gave him Strength. With Strength, Ren Zu’s life improved. He gained a reliable source of food and the power to protect himself. He took eagerly to fighting, defeating many Predicaments. But he soon suffered for it. Eventually, he discovered that Strength was not all-powerful: it required rest and recovery and could not be squandered at will.

Moreover, his strength alone was far too little against all the Predicament beasts together. Once his suffering had eased, Ren Zu reflected on what he had endured. He decided to sustain the most beautiful of the three Gu with his middle years, when he was in the prime of his life. Then the second Gu gave him Wisdom. With Wisdom, Ren Zu learned to think and reflect, beginning to accumulate experience. He discovered that Wisdom was often more effective than Strength. With both, he overcame challenges that had once been beyond him and killed more Predicaments. He ate their flesh and drank their blood, tenaciously surviving. But the good times did not last. Ren Zu grew old, older and older. This was because he had offered his youth and middle years to Strength Gu and Wisdom Gu.
Once a person grows old, their muscles waste away and their mind slows.
“Human, what can you still give us? You have nothing left to offer.” Once Strength Gu and Wisdom Gu realised this, they abandoned him without compassion.

Ren Zu had lost Strength and Wisdom. The Predicaments found him again and surrounded him. He was old and could no longer run. All his teeth had fallen out; he could not even chew wild fruit or edible greens. He collapsed helplessly to the ground, Predicaments crowding all around. His heart filled with despair. Just then, the third Gu spoke. “Human, sustain me, and I can free you from these Predicaments.”

Ren Zu said through his tears, “Gu, what could I possibly have left? Look, Strength Gu and Wisdom Gu have both abandoned me. All I have is my old age. Compared with youth and middle age, it may be worth little, but if I offer even that to you, my life will end immediately. Though the Predicaments surround me, I will not die just yet. I want to live a little longer, even if only for a single second. So go. I can no longer sustain you.”
But the Gu said, “Of the three of us, I ask for the least. Human, all you need to do is give me your heart.”
“Then I’ll give you my heart,” Ren Zu said. “But, Gu, what can you give me? In this desperate situation, even if Strength Gu and Wisdom Gu returned to my side, they could not change anything.”

Beside Strength Gu, this Gu had the frailest form: nothing more than a tiny point of light. Beside Wisdom Gu, it was the dimmest, giving off only a faint white glow, devoid of splendour or brilliance. But when the human gave his heart to the Gu, it suddenly blazed with boundless light. Amidst that radiance, the Predicaments cried out in terror: “It’s Hope Gu! Retreat! We fear hope most of all!” The beasts immediately fled in panic.
Ren Zu stared, eyes wide and mouth agape. From that moment on, he understood: when facing predicaments, give your heart to hope.

At that moment, the stream of Hope Gu gathered and entered Fang Yuan’s body. Under the external pressure, they clustered of their own accord roughly ten centimetres below his navel. Fang Yuan immediately felt the pressure ease slightly. He stepped forward. With every step, more Hope Gu rose from the flower field, entered his body, and joined the mass of light.
The mass grew larger and brighter. But across the river, the elder in charge's brow furrowed.
“There seem to be rather few Hope Gu.” At the sight, the hearts of the many elders who had been discreetly watching Fang Yuan sank.
The Clan Leader's brow furrowed as well. These were certainly not the signs one would expect from Grade A aptitude.
Fang Yuan continued forward against the pressure.
“Fewer than ten steps means no aptitude. Ten to twenty is Grade D; twenty to thirty, Grade C; thirty to forty, Grade B; forty to fifty, Grade A. So far, I have taken twenty-three steps.”
At his twenty-seventh step, he seemed to hear a boom. The mass of light in his abdomen, between his kidneys, had reached its limit and suddenly burst.

The burst occurred entirely within Fang Yuan’s body; no one else could detect it. Only he experienced its mysterious, earth-shaking wonder. In an instant, the fine hairs all over his body stood on end and his pores closed tightly. His mind drew taut like a bowstring pulled back to its limit. Immediately afterward, his mind went blank and his whole body relaxed, as though he had fallen into the clouds. The tension eased, his body hair settled, and every pore opened. All at once, a light sheen of perspiration covered his skin.

Though it takes time to describe, the process was exceedingly brief. It came swiftly and ended just as abruptly. Fang Yuan was dazed for only an instant before collecting himself. He quietly concentrated and examined within. An aperture had appeared out of nowhere in his abdomen, below his navel and between his kidneys.
His aperture had opened successfully.
This was the hope of immortality.

The aperture was spherical, its surface enclosed by a membrane of flowing white light. Though lodged within Fang Yuan’s body, it did not share space with his internal organs. You could call it infinitely vast; you could just as well call it infinitely small. Some called it the Purple Palace. Others, the Flowery Pool. Most, however, called it the Primeval Sea Aperture. This was what the Hope Gu had become: burst apart, then drawn together into that very membrane. It was precisely this membrane of light that held the aperture together and kept it from collapsing.

Within the aperture lay the primeval sea. The water lay smooth as a mirror, a sheet of jade green, yet viscous beyond any water, carrying a copper lustre. This was the bronze primeval essence that only a First Revolution Gu Master possessed, condensed together. Commonly, it was called the bronze sea. The surface of the sea did not reach half the height of the aperture. It stood at only forty-four percent. With his Grade C aptitude, this was as much as his aperture could hold. Every drop of that water was primeval essence. It represented the condensing of Fang Yuan’s essence, qi, and spirit, and stood for the vital potential he had accumulated over fifteen years.

It was with this primeval essence that a Gu Master drove his Gu worms. From this moment on, Fang Yuan had formally stepped into the ranks of First Revolution Gu Masters. The aperture was open. No more Hope Gu flowed into his body. Fang Yuan withdrew his attention. He felt only that the pressure ahead was as thick and solid as a wall, and that he could not advance another step.
“Just as in my previous life.” He gave a faint, indifferent smile at the result.
“Can you go no further?” the Academy Elder called from across the river, still clinging to that one chance in ten thousand.
Fang Yuan simply turned and walked back, letting his actions answer for him. At that, even the youths finally caught on. At once there was a rising buzz, and the crowd erupted.
“What? Fang Yuan walked twenty-seven steps?”
“So he only has Grade C aptitude?!”
“Unbelievable. A genius like him, only of Grade C?”
An uproar swept through the crowd.

“Brother…” In the crowd, Gu Yue Fang Zheng raised his head and stared in shock at Fang Yuan wading back across the river. He could not believe the scene before him. His own elder brother was only of Grade C?
He had always believed his elder brother would be of Grade A aptitude. No-not only he. His uncle and aunt, and many others in the clan, had believed the same. And yet now, this was the result!
“Damn it. Only of Grade C!” The Clan Leader clenched his fists in secret and let out a deep sigh. His disappointment was plain beyond words.
Among the elders watching in secret, some knitted their brows, some lowered their heads in discussion, and some tipped their heads back and let out a long sigh.
“Could there be an error in the test?”
“How could it be? The method is accurate beyond compare. With us watching throughout, even cheating would be difficult.”
“But then how do you explain his earlier performance, and his talent?”

“The higher a youth’s primeval sea aptitude, the more he will indeed display qualities beyond the ordinary. Intelligence, comprehension, memory, strength, agility, and so on. But the reverse does not hold. Those qualities do not mean the aptitude must be high. In the end, the test result is what decides.”
“Haa. The greater the hope, the greater the disappointment. The Gu Yue Clan grows worse with every generation.”

The icy river water soaked through his socks, cold enough to bite at the bone. Fang Yuan walked on, his face as expressionless as ever. The distance closed, and he could clearly see the heavy look on the Academy Elder’s face. He could feel keenly the eyes of more than a hundred youths fixed on him. In those eyes there was astonishment, shock, mockery, delight at his misfortune, sudden understanding, and cold indifference. The scene was identical, and it drew Fang Yuan’s thoughts back to his previous life.

Back then, he had felt as if the sky had come down. He had missed his footing crossing the river and gone sprawling, soaked through and out of his wits. Not one person had put out a hand to help him. Those disappointed, indifferent faces and eyes had been like sharp knives slicing his heart away piece by piece. His thoughts had run wild, and a dull ache had spread through his chest. It was like falling from the clouds to the ground. The higher one stood, the harder one fell.

But in this life, standing once more in such a scene, Fang Yuan was utterly calm. He thought of that legend. When predicaments come, entrust your heart to hope. And now that hope lay within his own body. It was not a great hope, but it was already better than those with no aptitude for cultivation at all. If others were disappointed, let them be. What of it?

Five hundred years of living had taught him one truth: what makes a life interesting is the pursuit of one’s own dreams. There is no need to demand that others withhold their disappointment, or grant their approval.
Go your own way, and let others be disappointed and disapprove.
“Haa…” The Academy Elder let out a deep sigh, then called again. “Next. Gu Yue Fang Zheng.”
No one answered.
“Gu Yue Fang Zheng!” The Elder shouted, and his voice went humming and echoing through the karst cavern.

“Ah? Here, I’m here!” Fang Zheng tore himself free of his shock and hurried forward, only to stagger underfoot. He went straight over in a tumble and fell with a splash, rolling, as luck would have it, right into the river.
At once, laughter broke out across the whole cavern.
“The Fang brothers. Nothing more than this.” The Clan Leader gave a cold snort, and a certain distaste for Gu Yue Fang Zheng rose in him as well.

“Now I’ve really disgraced myself!” Fang Zheng thrashed hard a few times in the water, but he could not get to his feet at all, for the riverbed was slick. All his effort only made him look clumsier. Burst after burst of laughter reached his ears, and he grew more flustered still.

But just then, he felt a great force yank at him, and his head came up out of the water at last. His body found its balance. He wiped his face in a sorry state and looked to see that it was his elder brother, Fang Yuan, gripping him by the collar and hauling him up.
“Brother…” He opened his mouth to speak and only choked on water, which set off a violent fit of coughing.
“Haha, the Fang brothers, a matched pair of wretches!” Someone on the bank jeered aloud.

The laughter grew louder still, and the Academy Elder did not step forward to stop it. His brow furrowed deeply, filled with disappointment. Fang Zheng was at a complete loss, and then his elder brother’s voice came at his ear. “Go on. The road to the future will be interesting.”

Fang Zheng’s mouth fell open in surprise. Fang Yuan had his back to the crowd just then, so no one on the bank could see clearly. But Fang Zheng felt his calm distinctly, and saw that as he spoke, the corners of his mouth even curved upward, revealing a faint smile, thoughtful and amused.
“He’s obviously only of Grade C aptitude. So why is my elder brother still this calm?” Fang Zheng filled with doubt in spite of himself.
Fang Yuan said nothing further. He patted Fang Zheng on the back, turned, and walked away. Still dazed, Fang Zheng walked towards the flower field.

“I’d never have thought my elder brother could be this calm. If it were me, I’m afraid…” His head was down and he walked on without thinking, not knowing that he was in the middle of staging a miraculous performance.
By the time he came to himself with a start, he was standing deep in the flower field, at a distance no one before him had reached.
Forty-three steps!
“Heavens, Grade A aptitude!!!” The Academy Elder cried out, all composure gone.
“Grade A? Truly Grade A?!”
“Three years! At last the Gu Yue Clan has produced another genius of Grade A aptitude!”
The elders watching in secret cried out at the same moment, their dignity abandoned entirely.
“Mm. The Fang lineage split off from our Chi lineage to begin with, so this Gu Yue Fang Zheng will be taken in by my Chi lineage.” Gu Yue Chi Lian announced it on the spot.

“How could that be? What virtue, what ability do you have, Chi Lian, you old geezer? Leading other people’s children astray is the only talent you have. Better to hand the child to me, Gu Yue Mo Chen, to bring up.” Gu Yue Mo Chen reacted as if a jolt had gone through him, and roared at once.

“None of you will contend for him. No matter who grooms this child, none will do it as well as this Clan Leader in person. Anyone with an objection is opposing me, Gu Yue Bo!” The Clan Leader’s eyes were bloodshot; he had gone into a frenzy. His earlier disappointment and dejection were swept away.
Soon, a week had passed.

“Man is the spirit of all things, and Gu are the essence of heaven and earth. In this world, there are thousands upon thousands of kinds of Gu, countless beyond reckoning. They live all around us: in ore and soil, in thickets of grass, and even within the bodies of wild beasts.”

“As humanity thrived and multiplied, our forebears gradually discovered the profound mysteries of Gu worms. Those who have opened their apertures and use their own primeval essence to feed, refine, and manipulate these Gu to achieve various ends are collectively known as Gu Masters.”
“Seven days ago, during the Aperture Opening Ceremony, all of you successfully opened your apertures and condensed your primeval essence seas. As of now, you are all First Revolution Gu Masters.”
In the village academy, the Academy Elder spoke with confident composure.
Before him, fifty-seven youths sat upright, each listening with rapt attention.
The wonder and power of Gu Masters had long taken root in the youths’ hearts, so everything the elder taught left them completely captivated.

At that moment, a youth raised his hand. After the elder gave his permission, he stood and asked, “My lord Academy Elder, I have known since I was very young that Gu Masters are divided into First Revolution, Second Revolution, and so on. Could you explain it to us in detail?”

The Academy Elder, Gu Yue Shi, nodded and waved his hand for the youth to sit down. “Gu Masters have nine revolutions in total. From lowest to highest, they are First Revolution, Second Revolution, Third Revolution, all the way to Ninth Revolution. Within each major realm, there are four minor stages: initial, middle, upper, and peak. You have just become Gu Masters, so you are all at First Revolution, initial stage.”

“If you cultivate diligently from now on, your cultivation will naturally rise, and advancing to Second Revolution or Third Revolution will also be possible. Of course, the higher your aptitude, the greater the chance of advancement.”

“With Grade D aptitude, the primeval sea occupies twenty to thirty percent of the aperture; such people usually reach no higher than First Revolution or Second Revolution. With Grade C aptitude, the primeval sea occupies forty to fifty percent; such people usually stall at Second Revolution, with only a tiny fraction lucky enough to break through to Third Revolution, initial stage. With Grade B aptitude, the primeval sea occupies sixty to seventy percent; such people can cultivate to Third Revolution, and even as high as Fourth Revolution. With Grade A aptitude, the primeval sea occupies eighty to ninety percent and is abundant; naturally, such people possess the highest talent and are most suited to Gu Master cultivation, capable of reaching Fifth Revolution.”

“As for Gu Masters of Sixth Revolution and above, every single one is a legend. I am not too clear on the specifics myself. Our Gu Yue Clan has never produced a Sixth Revolution Gu Master, but we have had Fourth Revolution and Fifth Revolution Gu Masters before.”
The youths all pricked up their ears, listening intently with eyes shining bright.
Many could not help but look towards Gu Yue Fang Zheng, who sat in solemn posture in the first row. This was a Grade A aptitude, after all. Their gazes were filled with envy and jealousy.
At the same time, some gazes drifted towards the corner in the very last row of the classroom.
In that corner by the window, Gu Yue Fang Yuan was sprawled over his desk, fast asleep and snoring soundly.
“Look, he’s still sleeping,” someone whispered.
“He’s been sleeping through classes for a week straight. Hasn’t he recovered yet?” someone said with a sneer.
“More than that. I heard he doesn’t even return home at night, wandering all around the outskirts of the village.”

“People have seen him more than once at night, hugging a wine jar and dead drunk outside. Luckily, in recent years, the village surroundings have been cleared, so it is relatively safe.” The classmates huddled and whispered among themselves, and all kinds of hearsay spread rapidly.
“Alas, the blow was truly too great. He carried the title of a genius for so many years; who would have thought that in the end, he would only be a Grade C?” he chuckled bitterly.

“If it were just that, it would be one thing. But his own younger brother was tested as a Grade A, and now he is the centre of attention, enjoying the best treatment. The younger brother is high in the heavens while the older brother is down in the dirt, tsk tsk...”
As the murmurs around him grew louder and louder, the Academy Elder's brow furrowed deeper.
In the entire classroom, the youths all sat straight and proper, radiating youthful vigour; this made Fang Yuan, who lay sprawled asleep over his desk, stand out even more glaringly.

“A whole week has passed, and he is still so dispirited. Humph, I must have misjudged him back then. How could such a person possibly be a genius.” The elder snorted coldly with displeasure in his heart. He had already spoken to Fang Yuan about this situation many times, but it had no effect at all. Fang Yuan continued to do as he pleased. He slept through every lesson, which gave the Academy Elder a terrible headache and much annoyance.

“Forget it, he is just Grade C anyway. He cannot even withstand a blow like this. With a temperament like that, even if he were nurtured, he could hardly amount to anything; it would instead be a waste of the clan's resources.” The elder was thoroughly disappointed in Fang Yuan.
Fang Yuan was only of Grade C aptitude. In comparison, his younger brother, Fang Zheng, possessed Grade A aptitude; he was the one truly worth the clan's greatest efforts to nurture.

As he thought this, the Academy Elder continued aloud with the previous topic. “In our clan's history, many strong figures have appeared. Among them, there have been two Fifth Revolution experts. One was the first-generation clan leader, our founding ancestor, who established the Gu Yue Village. The other was the fourth-generation clan leader. His natural talent was outstanding, and he cultivated all the way to the realm of a Fifth Revolution Gu Master. If not for that despicable and shameless demon, the Flower-Wine Monk, launching a sneak attack, he might have advanced to Sixth Revolution. Alas...”
At this point, the Academy Elder let out a deep sigh.
Below the lectern, the youths all cried out, filled with righteous indignation.
“It’s all that Flower-Wine Monk’s fault; he was too sinister and cunning.”
“It’s a pity our fourth-generation clan leader was so kind-hearted and benevolent, yet died in his prime.”
“I only hate that I wasn’t born a few hundred years earlier. Otherwise, if I had met that demon, I would certainly have fought him to the death to expose his vile nature.”
There was not a single Gu Yue Clansman who did not know the story of the fourth-generation clan leader and the Flower-Wine Monk.

The Flower-Wine Monk was also a Fifth Revolution Gu Master, a notorious sexual predator who had committed evil for many years and was infamous in the demonic path at that time. Several hundred years ago, he made his way to Qing Mao Mountain and attempted to commit crimes in the Gu Yue Village, but was seen through by the fourth-generation clan leader. After an earth-shaking battle, the Flower-Wine Monk was beaten to his knees, begging for mercy. The fourth-generation clan leader, kind-hearted and benevolent, intended to spare his life. Instead, the Flower-Wine Monk suddenly launched a sneak attack, gravely wounding the fourth-generation clan leader.
The clan leader was consumed by rage and killed the Flower-Wine Monk on the spot. However, he subsequently succumbed to his severe wounds and departed from this mortal world.
Therefore, in the hearts of all Gu Yue Clansmen, the fourth-generation clan leader was a heroic figure who had sacrificed himself for the village.
“Flower-Wine Monk, huh...” Woken by the denunciations in the classroom, Fang Yuan opened his bleary, sleepy eyes.

He gave a long, lazy stretch, and in his heart he could not help but feel resentful. “Where on earth did this Flower-Wine Monk die? Why have I searched all around the village and still haven’t found his treasure?”

In his memory, about two months from now, a clan Gu Master who got drunk over a broken heart would lie dead drunk outside the village. The rich aroma of wine spreading in all directions would unexpectedly attract a Liquor Worm.

The Gu Master was overjoyed and tried to catch it. The Liquor Worm fled in panic, but the Gu Master chased closely without letting up; following its trail, he discovered a hidden cave entrance leading underground.

A Liquor Worm is a very precious kind of Gu. Still flushed with wine, that Gu Master risked entering the cave and reached a hidden underground cavern. There, he discovered the skeletal remains of the Flower-Wine Monk, along with the treasure left behind.
After the Gu Master returned to the village and reported all his findings, it immediately caused a great stir throughout the entire clan.

That Gu Master also benefited greatly from this fortune; his cultivation grew increasingly outstanding, even changing the heart of the lover who had once abandoned him. For a time, he became a prominent figure.

“What a pity that I only heard a general outline back then and didn’t know the exact location. At that time, I never thought there would be a day when I would be reborn. Flower-Wine Monk, where on earth did you die?”

Over these past few days, he had bought a lot of wine and wandered idly around the village every night. He wanted to use the redolence of the wine to lure the Liquor Worm into showing itself. Unfortunately, there was no sign of the creature at all, and the result was deeply disappointing.

“If I could find that Liquor Worm and refine it into my vital Gu, it would be far better than the clan’s Moonlight Gu. In the blink of an eye, it is already April; time waits for no man.” Fang Yuan sighed, turning his gaze out the window.
Under blue sky and white cloud, green mountains stretched away without end. Close by lay a bamboo grove.
This was the spear bamboo found only on Qing Mao Mountain, each stalk straight as a line, its tip sharp as a spearhead.
Not far off, the woods had come into new leaf. The tender buds formed a spread of yellow-green. From time to time, pretty, colourful little birds alighted on the branches.
A spring wind blew in, carrying the clean scent of green hills and clear water.

Before he knew it, the lesson was drawing to a close. The Academy Elder finally announced, “This week, I have taught you how to meditate and examine the primeval sea within your apertures, as well as how to sit cross-legged and circulate the primeval essence inside your bodies. Now, it is time to refine your vital Gu. Once this class dismisses, you will go to the academy’s Gu chamber to choose a Gu worm. Once selected, return home to cultivate in seclusion. Only after you have refined your Gu may you return to the academy to resume your lessons. At the same time, this will be your first assessment. Whoever takes first place will receive a generous reward of twenty primeval stones.”
A cry went up, and the whole classroom burst into cheers.
“Finally, it’s time to refine a Gu worm. So which Gu worm should I pick?” A sharp gleam flashed and vanished in Fang Yuan’s eyes.

Beside the academy stood a Gu chamber, not large, only sixty square metres in size. In the cultivation of a Gu Master, Gu worms are the ultimate key to strength. As soon as lessons ended, the excited youths swarmed towards the Gu chamber.

“Queue up, come in one by one!” A stern shout rang out. Guards were naturally stationed outside the Gu chamber door. The youths went in one by one, and then came out. It was Fang Yuan's turn to enter.

Inside, he saw that there was far more to the room than met the eye. The four walls were carved into recesses, inset square compartments densely packed and crowding one after another. They varied in size: the largest was no bigger than an earthenware cooking pot, and the smallest was no smaller than a fist. Within the tightly packed compartments sat a vast array of vessels: grey stone basins, vibrant green jade plates, delicate grass cages, and earthenware braziers. In these vessels were kept all kinds of Gu worms.
Some Gu worms were silent; others chirped, clucked, and rustled, their sounds mingling in a symphony of life.

“Gu worms are likewise divided into nine revolutions, corresponding to the nine revolutions of Gu Masters. The Gu worms here are all First Revolution Gu worms.” Fang Yuan surveyed the chamber, comprehending at a single glance. Generally, a First Revolution Gu Master can only use First Revolution Gu worms. Should they attempt to activate a Gu of a higher revolution than their own, they will often pay a devastating price.

Moreover, Gu worms require constant sustenance; the cost of nurturing a higher-level Gu is often more than a lower-level Gu Master can afford. The very first Gu worm a Gu Master refines carries great significance; known as their vital Gu, it is inextricably bound to their life force. Should it perish, the Gu Master will inevitably suffer grievous damage.

Fang Yuan sighed inwardly even as he walked straight towards the wall on his left. Slightly higher up on the wall, on one of the levels, stood a row of silver plates. Upon each plate rested a Gu worm. This Gu worm was crystal clear and curved like a crescent moon, resembling a piece of blue crystal. Set against the silver base, it revealed a wisp of clear and ethereal aura.

Its name was Moonlight Gu, the Gu Yue Clan's signature Gu. The vast majority of clansmen choose it as their vital Gu. It is not a natural Gu worm, but one cultivated through the Gu Yue Clan's secret method. Found nowhere else, it can be said to be the emblem of the Gu Yue Clan. All were First Revolution Moonlight Gu; the differences between them were extremely subtle. Fang Yuan picked one at random and took it in his hand.

The Moonlight Gu was very light, no heavier than a thin sheet of paper. Occupying only a small patch of his palm, it was the size of an ordinary jade pendant. Holding it in his hand, Fang Yuan could see the lines of his palm through it. After a final glance confirming nothing was amiss, Fang Yuan slipped it into his pocket and left the Gu chamber.

Outside the Gu chamber, the long queue was still lined up. Seeing Fang Yuan walk out, the next youth hurried eagerly into the chamber. Had it been anyone else, upon obtaining a Gu worm, their first instinct would be to rush home and refine it. Fang Yuan did not hurry; his mind remained fixed on that Liquor Worm. The Liquor Worm is more precious; although the Moonlight Gu is a specialty of Gu Yue Village, it lacks the sheer utility a Liquor Worm offers a Gu Master.
Leaving the Gu chamber, Fang Yuan went directly to the wine shop.

“Shopkeeper, two jars of aged wine.” Fang Yuan fished in his pocket and laid his last fragments of primeval stone on the counter. For the past few days, he would come here to buy wine, then wander the outskirts of the village, searching for a way to lure that Liquor Worm into the open.
The shopkeeper was a short, fat, middle-aged man, his face shining with oil. After these past days, he had already come to remember Fang Yuan.

“Honoured customer, you're here.” As he spoke, he stretched out his stubby, fat hand and deftly swept away Fang Yuan's primeval stone fragments. He hefted them in his palm, and finding the weight sufficient, his smile grew a touch more cordial.

Primeval stones are the currency of this world, used to measure the value of all commodities. They are also the condensed essence of heaven and earth, capable of being directly absorbed to aid a Gu Master's cultivation. Possessing both monetary and commodity attributes, they are remarkably similar to gold on Earth. Earth once utilised a gold standard; in this world, it is a primeval stone standard. Compared to gold, the purchasing power of primeval stones is even more astonishing. However, no amount of primeval stones can withstand Fang Yuan's continuous consumption like this.
“Two jars of wine every day for seven days straight. The primeval stones I accumulated are almost all spent.” Carrying two jars out of the shop, Fang Yuan furrowed his brows slightly.

Once a Gu Master, a person can directly extract pure primeval essence from primeval stones to replenish the primeval sea within their aperture. Therefore for Gu Masters, primeval stones are not only a currency, but also an aid in cultivation. With sufficient primeval stones, cultivation speed can increase significantly; this can more or less compensate for shortcomings in aptitude.

“Tomorrow, I will lack the primeval stones to purchase wine, yet the Liquor Worm has still failed to show itself. Must I truly refine the Moonlight Gu into my vital Gu?” Fang Yuan felt a pang of reluctance.

Leaving the wine shop with two jars of wine in hand, Fang Yuan pondered as he walked: “The academy elder stated that the first to refine their vital Gu in this assessment would be rewarded with twenty primeval stones. Presently, many are likely exerting every ounce of effort at home, refining their Gu worms to vie for first place. Alas, refining a vital Gu severely tests one's aptitude. Those blessed with superior talent possess an immense advantage. Given my Grade C aptitude, lacking alternative means, I fundamentally have no hope of victory.”
Just then, Gu Yue Fang Zheng's voice came from behind him: “Brother, you've really come back to the wine shop to get drunk again! Come with me; our uncle and aunt wish to see you.”
Fang Yuan stopped and turned. He observed that his brother no longer spoke with a lowered head as before.
The brothers' gazes collided. A gust of wind howled past, lifting the elder brother's dishevelled black hair and fluttering the younger brother's robes.
A mere month, yet things remained while people had changed.

A week prior, the Aperture Opening Ceremony marked a momentous change for both brothers. The elder brother, Fang Yuan, plummeted from the clouds, the halo of genius mercilessly stripped away, while his younger brother began to radiate like a nascent star, slowly ascending. For the younger brother, Gu Yue Fang Zheng, this change bore earth-shattering significance.

The clan's high hopes, which had once been entrusted to his elder brother, now fell entirely upon his shoulders. He became the focus of the clan, drawing the gazes of envy and jealousy from all around.

He felt as though he had suddenly stepped out of a dark corner into a paradise filled with light. Each morning when he woke, it seemed he was living a beautiful dream. The vastly different treatment still left him somewhat incredulous. At the same time, it left him profoundly ill at ease. Unaccustomed to being the centre of attention, he was at a loss as to how to handle it.

In the past, he had been a youth of utter obscurity, never pointed at and whispered about wherever he went. Now, as he walked along the road and heard the discussions of others, his face would burn; he did not know what to do with his hands or feet, and he avoided their gazes, almost forgetting how to walk. A dozen or so days passed, and he grew thinner, yet the fire within his chest burned ever more vigorously. Deep within him, something called confidence began to grow.

“So this is how my brother used to feel. Wonderful, yet painful!” He could not help thinking of Fang Yuan. How had his brother dealt with all those comments and all that attention?
