Instinctively, he began to imitate him, pretending to be expressionless, but he swiftly realised he was not cut out for it.

At times in the academy, a single exclamation from a girl could send him blushing crimson. On the road, the teasing of aunties would send him fleeing in disarray time and again. Like an infant learning to walk, he tottered as he adapted to his new life.

In this process, he inevitably heard rumours about his brother: dejected and dissolute, turned to drink, absent from home at night, sleeping heavily in the academy. At first, he was utterly shocked: his own brother, a being of such power and genius, had come to this?!

Yet gradually, he began to understand somewhat. Elder brother, too, was but an ordinary man; faced with such setbacks and blows, dejection was inevitable. With this understanding came a faint, indescribable thrill of pleasure within Fang Zheng. It was a pleasure he dearly wished to deny, yet it undeniably existed.
His elder brother, once lauded as a genius who had loomed over him like a shadow, now seemed so downfallen and dejected. Seen from the other side, did this not all the more attest to his own growth?
“I am exceptional. That alone is the truth!” he told himself.
Therefore, seeing Fang Yuan with wine jars in hand, his hair dishevelled and clothes untidy, Gu Yue Fang Zheng inwardly heaved a great sigh of relief, his breathing inexplicably eased.
Yet he said: “Brother, you can't drink anymore, you can't go on like this. Don't you know how worried those who care about you will be? You need to pull yourself together!”
Fang Yuan remained expressionless, saying nothing.

The brothers' eyes met. Gu Yue Fang Zheng's eyes shone bright, revealing a sharp intent. His elder brother Fang Yuan's eyes, by contrast, were dark and profound, like a secluded ancient pool. Such eyes made Fang Zheng feel an inexplicable pressure. Before long, he subconsciously averted his gaze, looking to the side.
But the moment he came to himself, anger surged in his heart. An anger towards himself.
“What's wrong with me? Don't I even have the courage to look my brother in the eye? I have changed! I have completely changed!” he thought.

With this thought, his gaze sharpened again and swept back. But Fang Yuan was no longer looking at him. Carrying a jar of wine in each hand, he walked past him and said flatly: “What are you standing there for? Let's go.”

Fang Zheng's breathing faltered. The breath he had built up in his chest now had nowhere to go, leaving him with an inexpressible frustration. Seeing his brother already walking away, he could only hasten after him.
Only this time, his head was no longer lowered. It was raised, facing the sunset. His gaze was fixed upon his own feet, which trod step by step upon the shadow of his brother Fang Yuan.
Westward the red sun sank, yet had not wholly set.
The sky still held a little light, yet all things seemed veiled in grey. Through the window, the distant mountains could be seen slowly sinking into heavy, thickening darkness.
Within the living room, the light was dim. Uncle and Aunt sat high upon the seats of honour, their faces and expressions shrouded in shadow, scarcely to be discerned.

Seeing the two jars of wine Fang Yuan had brought, Uncle Gu Yue Dong Tu's brow furrowed deeply. He said, “How time flies, you are both fifteen already. You both possess Gu Master aptitude, Fang Zheng especially. Your aunt and I are proud of you both. I have set aside six primeval stones for each of you. Take them, brothers. Refining Gu worms consumes primeval essence at a great rate. You shall have need of these stones.”
As he spoke, a servant came forward and handed each brother a small pouch.
Fang Yuan tucked the pouch away, saying nothing.

Fang Zheng at once loosened the drawstring and looked inside. Within lay six oval, grey-white primeval stones, translucent. His face flushed with gratitude. He stood and bowed to Uncle and Aunt. “Thank you, Uncle and Aunt. Your nephew is indeed in need of primeval stones to replenish his primeval essence. You raised your nephew to this age, and your kindness in raising him is engraved upon his heart, never to be forgotten.”
Uncle smiled and nodded.

Aunt hastily waved her hands and said gently to Fang Zheng, “Quick, sit, sit. Though you two were not born of us, we have always raised you as our own sons. That you can amount to something, we too feel proud. Alas, we have no children of our own. At times we think how fine it would be if you could truly become our children.”
These words carried a deep meaning. Fang Zheng did not catch it, but Fang Yuan faintly furrowed his brow.
Sure enough, Uncle went on, “Aunt and I have discussed it. We wish to adopt you into our household, to become a true family. Fang Zheng, are you willing?”

Fang Zheng was taken aback, but swiftly joy flooded his face and he agreed at once. “To speak truly, since my parents died, your nephew has longed for a family of his own. To become one family with Uncle and Aunt, nothing could be better.”
Aunt's expression eased and she laughed. “Then you are our good son. Do you still call us Uncle and Aunt?”
“Father, Mother.” Fang Zheng understood and quickly corrected himself.
Uncle and Aunt both laughed heartily.
“Good son, not in vain have we raised you since you were five, a full ten years,” Aunt said, wiping tears from her eyes.
Uncle then turned his gaze upon the silent Fang Yuan. “Fang Yuan, what about you?”
Fang Yuan shook his head and said nothing.
“Brother,” Fang Zheng began, wishing to persuade him, but Uncle deterred him.

Uncle's tone did not change. He said again, “Since it is so, Fang Yuan, we will not force you. But you are already fifteen; you ought to set up your own household. Thus it will be convenient for you to inherit your branch of the Fang lineage. Uncle has prepared two hundred primeval stones, as support for you.”
“Two hundred primeval stones!” Fang Zheng's eyes widened at once. He had never seen so many primeval stones, and could not help showing envy.
Yet Fang Yuan still shook his head.
Fang Zheng was greatly puzzled. Uncle's face changed faintly, and Aunt's face darkened as well.

“Uncle, Aunt, if there is nothing else, your nephew will take his leave first.” Fang Yuan afforded them no chance to speak again. Leaving these words behind, he lifted his wine jars and walked straight out of the hall.
Fang Zheng stood up. “Father, Mother, brother cannot think it through for the moment. Why not let me persuade him?”

Uncle waved his hand and heaved a deliberate sigh. “Alas, this matter cannot be forced. That you should have such a heart, as your father I am already greatly comforted. Someone, take young master Fang Zheng down and settle him properly.”
“Then your son shall take his leave.” Fang Zheng withdrew, and the hall fell into silence.
The sun sank wholly behind the mountains, and the hall grew ever more gloomy.
After a long while, Uncle's cold voice came from the gloom. “It seems this little bastard Fang Yuan has seen through our scheme.”
Among Gu Yue Clan rules, there is a clear provision: the eldest son at sixteen possesses the qualification to inherit family property.
Fang Yuan's parents had already passed away, leaving behind a not inconsiderable inheritance, all of it being kept by Uncle and Aunt.
The value of this inheritance was not to be compared with a mere two hundred primeval stones.

If Fang Yuan were also adopted by Uncle and Aunt like Fang Zheng, he would have no qualification to inherit this inheritance. If Fang Yuan established his own household at fifteen this year, he would likewise not conform to the clan's regulation for inheritance.
“Fortunately, we have won over Fang Zheng, and Fang Yuan has only Grade C aptitude.” Uncle sighed again, feeling immense relief.
“Then Lord Husband, Fang Yuan plainly intends to go independent at sixteen, what ought we to do?” Aunt's voice grew urgent at the thought of that inheritance.

“Hmph, since he harbours ill intent, he can hardly blame us. So long as, before he goes independent, we seize on a grave fault of his and expel him from the household, we will strip him of his right to the inheritance.” Uncle snorted coldly.
“But this little bastard Fang Yuan is very clever, how would he commit a fault?” Aunt did not understand.

Uncle at once rolled his eyes and rebuked in a low voice, “How stupid you are! He will not commit a fault; can we not frame him? Let that girl Shen Cui seduce Fang Yuan first, then cry out that he has violated her. We catch them red-handed in the act, then slander him with drunken debauchery, a crime of utter depravity. Are you afraid we cannot expel Fang Yuan?”
“You still have a method, a brilliant stratagem!” Aunt was overjoyed at once.
A dense night descended, the stars, mostly veiled by drifting clouds, filling the sky. In the stockade, household after household gradually lit their lamps.
Gu Yue Fang Zheng was led into a room.

“Young Master Fang Zheng, this is a room this old servant specially tidied and vacated upon Master's personal instruction.” Granny Shen introduced it obsequiously, stooping, her face wreathed with flattering smiles.

Fang Zheng looked round, his eyes brightening. This room was more than twice as large as his former room. At its centre was a broad bed; by the window, a desk of sandalwood set with a fine brush, ink, paper and inkstone; the surrounding walls hung with exquisite ornaments. Even beneath his feet was not ordinary flooring, but a layer of soft, hand-made carpet.
From childhood to now, Fang Zheng had never lived in such a room. At once he nodded repeatedly. “This is very good, really quite fine. Thank you, Granny Shen.”
This Granny Shen was Aunt's most trusted person, managing all the servants in the household, a housekeeper in all but name.
Fang Yuan's personal maid Shen Cui was her daughter.

Granny Shen chuckled. “How could this old servant dare accept young master's thanks, it is as it should be, as it should be. Young master need only eat well and sleep well, if you want anything, shake the bell by the bedside, a servant will come up at once to await your orders. Master has instructed that in these days young master should devote himself wholly to cultivation; other trifling matters should be left to us servants to handle.”
A fresh surge of gratitude rose in Fang Zheng's heart. He said nothing more, only silently resolved within himself: “I must seize first place, and not disappoint Uncle and Aunt!”
The clouds above thickened, and with them the night deepened. The stars were all but veiled, save for a few that still glimmered faintly, struggling against the darkness.

“Uncle and Aunt should be plotting how to expel me from the household. In the previous life they secretly instigated servants to provoke me, then framed me, and in the end expelled me. I wonder what change there will be in this life.” Fang Yuan walked along the street, sneering coldly within his heart.
As for the true colours of Uncle and Aunt, he had seen through them long ago.
Yet it could be understood.
Man dies for wealth as birds die for food, whether on Earth or in this world, there are always those who trample upon kinship, friendship and love for the sake of benefit.
In truth, there was no kinship at all. Uncle and Aunt had taken the brothers in for no other reason than coveting the inheritance. Only the two brothers had repeatedly surprised them.

“All things are difficult at the beginning, and for me doubly so. I possess neither outstanding aptitude nor the guidance of any elder. In truth, I am starting from scratch. My parents' inheritance may yet serve as a great springboard. In the previous life, Uncle and Aunt seized that inheritance, and for that loss I squandered two whole years before I could cultivate to the peak of the First Revolution. In this life, that error shall not be repeated.”
So he went his way, pondering as he walked.
He did not remain in his lodgings, but, carrying two jars of wine, headed straight for the outside of the stockade.
The night sky grew ever more overcast, dark clouds veiling starlight, the mountain wind whistling with a rising howl, ever stronger.
Mountain rain was about to break.
Still, he must explore. His parents' inheritance could only be reclaimed when he was sixteen next year, while Flower-Wine Monk's treasure was something that might be obtained in the near term.
In the street, few folk were about. From houses by the roadside, dim light shone; some household refuse, leaves, and dust rolled along, blown by the wind, drifting aimlessly.
Fang Yuan's thin clothes could scarcely hold back this mountain wind, and he could not help but feel a chill.
He simply opened one of the jars he carried and took a small sip. Though it was turbid wine, once swallowed, warmth rose within him.
This was the first time in all these days that he had truly drunk at all.
The further from the stockade, the sparser the houses by the road, the dimmer the lights.
Ahead, gloom lay thicker. Wind pressed upon the mountain forest, branches swaying in the night, whistling as though beasts roared.
Fang Yuan's steps did not falter. He passed beyond the stockade gate and went on, his figure receding further and further into the dark road.
Behind him lay the myriad lights of home, bright and glorious.
Amid those lights there was a warm corner.

There, brother Fang Zheng sat at his desk, reviewing the notes taken in class. The room was bright with lamplight, solid walls keeping out the cold wind, and at his hand stood a cup of warm ginseng tea, steam curling and rising.
“Young Master Fang Zheng, the hot water for your bath is ready,” came Shen Cui's voice softly from outside the door.
Fang Zheng's heart stirred. “Then bring it in.”
Shen Cui entered, sashaying as she came, her face full of coquettish charm.

“This servant pays respects to Young Master Fang Zheng.” She gazed upon Fang Zheng with amorous eyes. Fang Yuan was only Grade C, but Fang Zheng was of Grade A aptitude. To latch onto him, that would be truly great fortune!
In the past few months, I have experienced the pain of life, and I have been struggling physically and mentally.

Life is like a balance scale, with reality on one end and the inner self on the other. For me the side of reality grew heavier and heavier until the scale tipped, and that is where the pain came from.
People often walk for so long that they get lost in the scenery along the way and forget why they set out in the first place.
That is what happened. In the midst of that pain I felt waves of bewilderment.
Since my last book was completed, I have been on a break, trying to find my direction and recover the reason I set out in the first place.

That was about five or six years ago. I had already been reading webnovels for a while. The first was A Journey to the Ethereal, then Blasphemy, Zhu Xian, Mad God, House of Beast Tamers, Boiling Beast Blood, Mount Shu, I Alone Am Immortal, and so on.

I had read a great many novels, but a knot of frustration built up in my chest. The protagonists I saw were almost always blessed with heaven defying fortune and were upright and noble in character. The villains were mostly foolish, deranged and ugly, their titles resounding, yet they were all paper tigers, impressive to look at until they met the protagonist, and then they wilted.
So I began to think that I wanted to see a truly great villain.
This villain would be uncompromising and solitary, proud, dark and decisive in killing, never weak in the knees. He would never hide his own evil, and he would have no false goodness at all.

At a glance you could tell he was utterly evil, his demonic aura overwhelming and his killing intent filling the air. What he was best at was trampling rules and slaughtering the famed righteous sects.

Alone, he would be an enemy to the whole world, sowing terror among all living things. He would be a great master of the demonic path, sometimes arrogant and domineering, sometimes sinister and cunning, sometimes cold and merciless, standing at the very pinnacle and looking down on the world with disdain, while every brave soul who dared to challenge him came to a miserable end.
He was cruel in his methods and perhaps even dabbled with Gu worms. In short, you could tell at a glance that he was no decent person at all.
So what should his name be... Super Demon King? Black Mountain Old Demon? Green Robe Ancestor?
No, no, no.
After thinking it over, I thought, why not call him Gu Zhen Ren?
As it happened, I needed an account on Qidian at the time, so this ID was born.

Some TV dramas always do it like this: the villain defeats the protagonist and is just one final lethal strike away from killing him. Then the villain starts rambling on and on, while the protagonist secretly gathers his strength for one last gamble, and every time he turns the tables and wins.

If the situation is reversed and the villain is the one at a disadvantage, it goes like this. The protagonist unleashes his power and the villain is beaten to the ground. Facing the protagonist's sword, the villain suddenly bursts into tears, wailing and swearing to mend his ways. The protagonist, who is kindhearted and benevolent, hesitates. At that moment the villain launches a desperate counterattack, but it fails. The protagonist, who sees every detail with perfect clarity, completely subdues him. His heart hardens at the same time, he shouts, despicable, shameless, vile, and finally kills the villain.

There are also villains who kidnap the protagonist's family and friends, and almost never succeed in using them as leverage. Even with a huge advantage, they somehow get defeated by the protagonist for all sorts of unavoidable reasons and in baffling ways.

It was about six years ago that I created the ID, Gu Zhen Ren, because I had a wish in my heart to see a truly evil archvillain. He would have his own way of doing things, rejected by the world, roaming free and unrestrained and disdaining any explanation. He would be decisive in killing, never trapped by feelings, and never weak in the knees even at the sight of a beautiful woman.
His dreaded name made the whole world tremble, and at the mere mention of him people paled.
Those who understood him admired him, revered him and loved him. Those who hated him gritted their teeth and used every means they had, only to make him much stronger.
He walked his own path, solitude wrapped around him, and his cold eyes could see through every falsehood.
When faced with criticism and rejection, he scoffed with disdain. When faced with hollow praise and flattery, he sneered in silence.
He could endure solitude. He could even enjoy it.
If he was not walking towards success, then he was walking towards destruction.

He was a warrior, walking alone through darkness on a solitary journey, cutting through every obstacle in his path. Nothing could stand in his way. If a god blocked his path, he would kill the god. If a Buddha blocked his path, he would kill the Buddha!

This dream had always been buried deep in my heart. During these years of writing, I thought several times about starting to write it, but nothing came of it in the end. I did not quite dare. I felt my skill was not yet good enough.
And so, so many years passed. I went through some things, and compared with when I first started writing, much of it is now a case of things remaining but people having changed.

The past was somewhat unbearable to look back on, and this dream was also hidden away in the dust of time, gradually forgotten by me. Even when I did remember it now and then, I felt I was not prepared enough and still lacked the ability to write such a cathartic story.

But these past few days I stopped walking forward and looked back, and I suddenly understood something. Life is not cooking. When you cook, you usually have the oil, salt, soy sauce and vinegar prepared beforehand, and only then do you start.
Life does not wait for you to be ready. Even when you think everything is ready, do you not still lack a wisp of east wind, that one final condition?
Life is always rushed. Many things happen suddenly with little to no preparation.
Fate is unpredictable and ever-changing. No one can tell what will happen tomorrow.
So I made a decision. Against the backdrop of the prophesied end of the world in 2012 drawing near, I would write a new book.
This book would be called Gu Zhen Ren.
No other title could suit it better.
This is a cause planted six years ago, bearing fruit in the present.
Giving the book the same name has no other meaning. It is not narcissism or arrogance, just a way to fulfil a dream. To realise that original dream and to recover that feeling that once moved me.
There is no doubt this book will invite controversy. From the perspective of the Dragon Sky community, this is what you would call having warped values.
Yes, I will say it plainly here. This is a book with warped values.

Because the protagonist of this book is a great villain who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals and never gives up, supremely evil. While the antagonists in this book are mostly great, glorious and upright young heroes, or reputable and honourable orthodox sects.

I know this will disappoint many people, but please try to understand. Those who abandon their principles the moment they see a beautiful woman, do they still have the bearing of a peerless demon king or a great boss of the demonic path?
That is just being lovesick.
That is right. This book will kill women, and beautiful women at that. It will kill them in great numbers and without restraint.

And it will never hold back. No matter what kind of existence it is, as long as it is an enemy. No matter how powerful he is, it will fight him. No matter how beautiful she is, it will kill her all the same.

Pat, pat, pat…
Rain fell heavily, hitting the verdant bamboo buildings with crisp sounds.
In the pond before the bamboo buildings, the water surface was pelted by raindrops, fish darted happily back and forth through the water, and water weeds swayed at the bottom.
Dark clouds lay thick, and the entire view was veiled by a dense, heavy curtain of rain.
In a somewhat gloomy room, the window stood open, and Fang Yuan gazed quietly at the downpour, a faint sigh escaping his heart. “Three days. Three nights already.”
Three nights before, he had carried two jars of wine out of the stockade and continued exploring the surroundings.
But deep into the night a downpour had begun.
To be drenched like a drowned rat was not worth mentioning; the crux was that in such conditions he could no longer explore anywhere.
Rain would swiftly wash away the smell of wine, and if he forced his way through the rain to explore, he would likely arouse suspicion.

Before, he had disguised himself as a frustrated drunkard to conceal his true motive. But one should never underestimate the wisdom of others; more often than not, only fools believe others to be foolish.
So, helpless, Fang Yuan could only bring his exploration to an end.
And once the rain began, it continued without cease. At times heavy, at times light, at times sparse, at times dense, yet it never stopped.

“At this rate, the Liquor Worm won’t be found anytime soon. To be safe, I can only set about refining the Moonlight Gu first. If in the course of refining I happen to find the Liquor Worm, best of all; if not, I shall have to make do with this. Yet such things are common enough. Heaven is unpredictable, as sudden as wind and rain. In this world, where is there a man whose every undertaking goes smoothly, perfect in every way?” Fang Yuan's state of mind was very steady. Five hundred years of experience had long since washed away what little impatience was in his nature to begin with.
He closed the window and the door, and sat cross-legged upon the bed. He slowly closed his eyes, and once his breathing was even, he let his consciousness sink.
The next moment, the scene of his own aperture appeared within his mind.
Though the aperture was lodged within his body, it was wondrous beyond measure, infinitely vast and infinitely small.
A membrane of light enclosed the aperture. The white membrane seemed very thin, yet it truly supported the aperture.
Within the aperture lay an ocean of primeval essence.

The seawater was bronze-green in colour; its surface was as still as a mirror, and its level stood at about half the aperture's height. The entire primeval sea occupied forty-four percent of the aperture.
This was the bronze primeval sea of a First Revolution Gu Master. Every drop of seawater was primeval essence. It was Fang Yuan's life force, condensed from his essence, qi, and spirit.
Every drop of primeval essence was precious because it was the root of a Gu Master, the source of power. Only by relying on primeval essence could a Gu Master refine and activate Gu worms.
Withdrawing his consciousness from the primeval sea, Fang Yuan opened his eyes and took out the Moonlight Gu from within his robes.
The Moonlight Gu lay quietly in his palm like a small blue crescent, exquisite and translucent.

At a thought from Fang Yuan, the primeval sea within his aperture at once churned, and a stream of primeval essence broke through the surface, drawn outside his body, pouring entirely into the Moonlight Gu.
The Moonlight Gu suddenly burst into a dim blue radiance, trembling faintly in Fang Yuan's palm, resisting the influx of his primeval essence.

Gu are the essence of heaven and earth, the cipher of the Great Dao, the vessels of law. They are also living beings, innately free and unrestrained, each possessing a will of their own. Now Fang Yuan sought to refine it, that is, to erase its will. Sensing this danger, the Moonlight Gu naturally resisted.
The process of refining was extremely arduous.
As bronze primeval essence flowed into the crescent, it first dyed the crescent's two tips green.
Then this bronze-green tint began to spread toward the middle of the crescent.

In less than three minutes, a pallor appeared upon Fang Yuan's face. A great amount of primeval essence poured ceaselessly into the Moonlight Gu, bringing wave after wave of marrow-draining weakness that assailed his heart and mind without end.
One percent, two percent, three percent… eight percent, nine percent, ten percent.

Ten minutes later, Fang Yuan's primeval sea had lost ten percent of its primeval essence. Yet upon the surface of the Moonlight Gu, like blue crystal, the two points of bronze-green at the crescent tips had expanded only a tiny area towards the middle.
The Moonlight Gu's resistance was extremely stubborn.
Fortunately Fang Yuan had long anticipated this and was not surprised, persisting in infusing primeval essence into the Moonlight Gu.
Ten percent, twenty percent, thirty percent.

Another twenty minutes passed, and the primeval sea within Fang Yuan's body retained only fourteen percent. On the Moonlight Gu, the bronze-green tint had expanded by a thread. Taken together, the two bronze-green patches covered about one twelfth of the Moonlight Gu's entire surface.
As for the remaining portion, it was still the Moonlight Gu's own pale blue.
“Refining Gu is truly difficult.” Seeing this, Fang Yuan sighed inwardly, cut off the supply of primeval essence, and refined the Moonlight Gu no further.

Half an hour into the refinement, the primeval sea within his aperture had been depleted by more than half, leaving only fourteen percent of primeval essence. Yet only one twelfth of the Moonlight Gu had been refined.

Moreover, what was even harder to accept was that the Moonlight Gu still emitted a dim blue glow. Though Fang Yuan had stopped refining, it had not stopped resisting, still purging his bronze primeval essence.

Fang Yuan could clearly feel the primeval essence that had flowed into the Moonlight Gu being purged bit by bit by the Moonlight Gu, dissipating outside his body. On the Moonlight Gu's surface, the bronze-green tint at the two crescent tips was also slowly shrinking.
At this rate of decrease, in about six hours the Moonlight Gu would be able to purge all of Fang Yuan's primeval essence. To refine the Gu worm again then would be no different from starting anew.

“Every act of refining Gu is like two armies at war: a positional war and a war of attrition. The Gu worm has only been refined by one twelfth, while thirty percent of my primeval essence had already been consumed. A Gu Master refining Gu must replenish the primeval essence of his primeval sea even as he continues refining without cease, consolidating the fruits of victory. Refining Gu tests not only skill in mobilising primeval essence, but also patience for a prolonged war.”
Fang Yuan thought as he took a primeval stone from his money pouch.
A Gu Master has two ways to replenish expended primeval essence.

One is natural recovery. Every so often, the primeval sea will automatically replenish primeval essence. For someone of Fang Yuan's Grade C aptitude, about four percent of primeval essence is recovered in an hour. In six hours, twenty-four percent of total primeval essence can be recovered.
The second method is to draw upon the natural primeval power within primeval stones.
Primeval stones are treasures of nature, condensing natural primeval essence that can be absorbed by Gu Masters.
Fang Yuan held the primeval stone in his hand, continuously drawing out natural primeval essence from within, pouring it into the primeval sea of his own aperture.
The fine lustre upon the primeval stone's surface slowly dimmed, while the level of Fang Yuan's primeval sea rose visibly.

About half an hour later, the primeval sea had recovered again to forty-four percent of its volume. At this point, the rising trend of the sea surface came to an abrupt halt. Though there was still space within the aperture, Fang Yuan could store no more primeval essence. This was the limitation of his Grade C aptitude.
From this, the important role of cultivation aptitude can be seen.
The higher the aptitude, the more primeval essence stored within the aperture, and the faster the natural recovery of primeval essence.

For Fang Yuan, to refine a Gu worm and consolidate his gains, he had to absorb primeval stones, because the speed at which his primeval essence naturally recovered could not compare with the speed at which the Moonlight Gu expelled primeval essence.

But for Fang Zheng of Grade A aptitude, he could replenish eight percent of primeval essence every hour. In six hours, he could recover forty-eight percent of total primeval essence, while the Moonlight Gu in the same six hours could only expel thirty percent of primeval essence.
He did not even need external aid such as primeval stones. Simply refining continuously like this, resting a few times in between, after a few days he could successfully refine the Moonlight Gu.

Therefore, Fang Yuan had known from the very beginning that in this assessment of refining the Moonlight Gu, he had no chance at all of seizing first place. This was not a matter of strength; aptitude was the decisive factor.
The second factor was primeval stones.
If primeval stones were abundant and one spared no expense, a person of Grade B aptitude might also surpass Grade A and seize first place.

“I have only six primeval stones in hand, not comparable to those like Gu Yue Mo Bei and Gu Yue Chi Cheng who have the support of elders behind them. My aptitude is only Grade C, also not comparable to Gu Yue Fang Zheng of Grade A aptitude. This assessment originally had not a shred of chance of victory. It would be better to split my focus and search for the Liquor Worm. If I can refine the Liquor Worm into my vital Gu, it would be far better than the Moonlight Gu. Mm? The sound of rain outside the window has softened; it seems to be letting up. This heavy rain has already fallen continuously for three days and three nights. It should stop by now.”
Fang Yuan put away the Moonlight Gu, got down from the bed, and was just about to open the window when a knock sounded at the door.

From outside the door came the voice of his personal maid Shen Cui. “Young Master Fang Yuan, it is your servant. This rain has fallen for three days continuously. Your servant has brought you some wine and food. Young master, eat and drink a little; it may ease some of your weariness and melancholy.”
